title: 红金饼干铁盒  (The Biscuit Tin)

segments.t: Morning sunshine pours through the open green shutters of Room 9. Qing spreads a clean kitchen towel across a small table while Mei and Zhou lean close over the waxed-cloth bundle. Listen to the whole scene first.
小晴，慢慢解开细绳——三十年的旧绳子一秒钟就会断！
厚亚麻布涂上蜂蜡真管用，里面连一滴湿气都没有。
掀开左边，再掀开右边……快看那些鲜亮的颜色！
等等——我认得那个红金铁盒子！我姑姑以前经常用它装节日杏仁饼干！
你们看盖子边缘缠着的那圈白布胶带。
铁盒子顶上用褪色的黑墨水写着一行字呢！
把我的老花镜拉下来——哦，在这儿呢——让我念念我们家的字迹！
周经理，盖子上的标签写着什么呀？
上面写着：八号房与九号房的时间胶囊，五月，留给晴朗的早晨。
他们真的把这个盒子留到九号房重新开放的这一周！
小晴，试试掀起盖子的一角——光用手能打开吗？
一毫米都动不了；三十年让铁盖子咬紧了，快叫老陈吧！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
小晴，慢慢解开细绳——三十年的旧绳子一秒钟就会断！

'Untie the string slowly, Qing—thirty-year-old twine could snap in a second!' "Jiekai" pairs "untie" with "open", and "yi miaozhong"—"one second"—leads straight into "jiu hui duan" ("will snap right away").
厚亚麻布涂上蜂蜡真管用，里面连一滴湿气都没有。
'Beeswax on heavy linen really works; not one drop of dampness reached the inside.' "Fengla" literally means "bee-wax", and the frame "lian yi di... dou meiyou" emphasises "not even a single drop".
掀开左边，再掀开右边……快看那些鲜亮的颜色！

'Fold back the left flap, fold back the right flap... look at those bright colours!' "Xiankai" means to fold back or lift open a flap or cover, while "zuobian" and "youbian" pair "left" and "right" with "side".
等等——我认得那个红金铁盒子！我姑姑以前经常用它装节日杏仁饼干！
'Wait—I know that red-and-gold tin box! My aunt kept holiday almond biscuits in it!' "Rende" means "recognise by sight", and "xingren binggan" joins "almond" with "dry-cake" for almond biscuits.
你们看盖子边缘缠着的那圈白布胶带。
'Look at the strip of white cloth tape wrapped around the rim of the lid.' "Gaizi" is a lid or cover, and "jiaodai" pairs "glue" with "ribbon" for adhesive tape.
铁盒子顶上用褪色的黑墨水写着一行字呢！
'There are words written in faded black ink right across the top of the tin!' "Tuise" literally means "shed colour"—"faded"—and "hei moshui" combines "black" with "ink-water" for black ink.
把我的老花镜拉下来——哦，在这儿呢——让我念念我们家的字迹！

'Pull down my glasses—no, here they are—let me read my family handwriting!' Reading glasses have a charming name in Mandarin: "laohuajing", literally "old-blurred-vision mirror", and "ziji" means "handwriting tracks".
周经理，盖子上的标签写着什么呀？
'What does the label on the lid say, Zhou?' "Biaoqian" is a label or tag, and Mandarin says "writes what" ("xie zhe shenme") where English asks "what does it say?".
上面写着：八号房与九号房的时间胶囊，五月，留给晴朗的早晨。
'It says: Time Capsule of Room Eight and Room Nine, May, for a sunny morning.' "Shijian jiaonang" pairs "time" with "capsule" word for word, and "liugei" means "left behind for".
他们真的把这个盒子留到九号房重新开放的这一周！
'They really left this box waiting for the week Room Nine opened again!' "Chongxin" joins "again" and "new" to mean "anew", pairing with "kaifang" ("open up").
小晴，试试掀起盖子的一角——光用手能打开吗？
'Try lifting the corner of the lid, Qing—will it open by hand?' "Shishi" doubles "try" for a gentle "give it a try", and "guang yong shou" means "using bare hands alone".
一毫米都动不了；三十年让铁盖子咬紧了，快叫老陈吧！
'Not a millimetre; thirty years made this tin lid tight, so call Chen!' "Dong bu liao" adds "bu liao" after "move" to show the lid cannot budge at all, even by "yi haomi"—one millimetre.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

一毫米都动不了；三十年让铁盖子咬紧了，快叫老陈吧！
Beneath the waxed linen gleams a red-and-gold almond biscuit tin waiting for Chen and his steady hands. See you next time.
回头见！
